product.name: Storeflow
product.goal: Make everyday selling, stock management, and store reporting simple for small and growing businesses.

technology.styling: Tailwind CSS with custom light-theme styles

rules: Keep screens clean and easy to scan.
Use large touch-friendly controls in checkout.
Keep important totals and actions easy to find.
Make the layout work on desktop, tablet, and mobile.

owner.description: Owns the business and can manage everything.

multi_tenant_security.model: Shared PostgreSQL database with tenant-scoped rows
rules: Every business-owned table must include tenant_id.
Every tenant-owned table must have Row Level Security enabled.
Users may only read or change rows for businesses where they are active members.
The frontend must never be trusted to enforce tenant isolation.
Tenant creation must go through the secure create_tenant_with_owner function.
PINs must be stored as hashes, never as plain text.
Sale prices and costs must be copied into sale_items so old sales never change.
multi_tenant_security.tenant_creation: Authenticated user calls create_tenant_with_owner, which creates the tenant, profile, and owner membership in one transaction.

tables.profiles: User profile details linked to Supabase Auth
tables.tenant_members: User membership and role for each business
tables.locations: Stores or branches belonging to a business
tables.products: Catalog items, barcodes, pricing costs, and tax rates
tables.product_prices: Prices that can vary by location and time
tables.inventory_balances: Current stock by location and product
tables.inventory_movements: Stock history for sales, purchases, returns, and adjustments
tables.sale_items: Frozen product details and prices from the time of sale
tables.payments: Cash, card, gift card, and split payment records
tables.employee_shifts: Shift times, registers, and cash drawer amounts

important_rules: Completed sales and stock deductions must happen in a database transaction.
Multiple payment rows represent a split payment.
Historical reporting uses sale_items.unit_cost and sale_items.unit_price.
Inventory movements provide the audit trail behind current balances.

new_business: User confirms their email if required.
User enters the store name and short name.
The secure database function creates the tenant and owner membership.
The user enters the store home screen.
sale: Cashier signs in or enters their PIN.
Cashier selects a register and starts a shift.
Cashier scans or taps products into the cart.
The system calculates subtotal, tax, discounts, and total.
Customer pays with one or more payment methods.
The sale is completed in a database transaction.
Stock is deducted and an inventory movement is recorded.
The receipt is emailed or printed.
stock_adjustment: Manager selects a location and product.
Manager enters the stock change and a reason.
The balance and movement ledger are updated together.
The change appears in the stock history.

hardware_interfaces.implementation_note: Keep WebHID, WebUSB, and Web Bluetooth code behind small interfaces so the checkout screen is not tied to one browser or device.

release_requirements: Apply the database migration to a Supabase project.
Set VITE_SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY in the deployment environment.
Keep the Supabase service-role key out of the frontend.
Run npm run build and npm run lint before deployment.
Test tenant isolation with two separate businesses.
Test checkout, payment, stock deduction, refunds, and role permissions.
Deploy the frontend to Vercel or Netlify.
comments: Add questions or changes to the COMMENTS section in IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.txt.
